Photo by Veronica Henri / Toronto Sun/Postmedia Article content In a recent Globe and Mail op-ed , members of the Jewish Faculty Network (JFN) assert that anti-Zionism is not antisemitism, that Jewishness is an exclusively religious identity that has nothing to do with statehood and that the debate between Zionist and anti-Zionist Jews has been going strong for 100 years. Their assertions are made without the benefit of reference to recent anonymous peer-reviewed survey research or anything more than a distorted understanding of modern Jewish history. Sign In or Create an Account or View more offers Article content Article content A 2026 survey of a representative sample of 626 Canadian Jewish adults found that 92 per cent of Canadian Jews support the existence of a Jewish state in Israel. They therefore fit the standard definition of “Zionist.” Eighty-six per cent of Canadian Jews think that supporting Israel is an important or essential part of their Jewish identity. Jewish statehood is thus a core element of Jewish identity for the overwhelming majority of Jews in Canada — and also, of course, for Jews in Israel (where about one-half of the world’s Jewish population resides) and elsewhere. Article content In contrast, just 60 per cent of Canadian Jews consider attending synagogue an important or essential part of Jewish identity; 59 per cent say the same about observing Jewish religious law. Article content All these findings are in line with results from a 2024 survey of 414 Canadian Jews and a 2018 survey of 2,335 Canadian who identify as Jewish by religion or ethnicity. Article content Members of the JFN are therefore wrong to claim that being Jewish is only a matter of religion and not a matter of statehood. Moreover, just as it is antisemitic to discriminate against Jews based on their religion, I believe it is antisemitic to erase support for the existence of a Jewish state as a core part of Jewish identify. Article content Article content Some Jews are anti-Zionists. They deny the need for the existence of a Jewish state. In Canada, a 2025 survey of 332 Jewish Canadians found that one per cent of Canadian Jews at the time regarded themselves as anti-Zionists, while the most recent 2026 survey of 625 Canadian Jews cited earlier puts the number at five per cent. The proportion of Jews who deny the need for Jewish statehood is thus tiny. Article content The representatives of the JFN correctly note that Reform Judaism in mid-19th century Germany held that Jewishness is exclusively a religious category. However, a century later, in the early 1940s, Reform Judaism officially endorsed the need for a Jewish state as the extent of the Holocaust became apparent. Article content Similarly, the members of the JFN cite the Jewish Labour Bund of Poland and Lithuania as a large and vigorous opponent of Zionism since its founding in 1897. This is an exaggeration . Most Bundists were killed in the Holocaust and many of those who survived became Zionists in the face of the Holocaust. In fact, Tel Aviv became one of the centres of Bundism after the Second World War. Advertisement 1 This advertisement has not loaded yet. Article content It should not surprise us that the JFN has written an op-ed arguing that anti-Zionism isn’t antisemitism. In the principles section of their website, they state that they oppose the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism which was accepted by Canada in 2019. It includes non-legally binding illustrative examples of what might constitute antisemitism, including, “D enying the Jewish people their right to self-determination.” Article content Notably, the JFN’s “principles” page on their website lacks any mention of the horrific attacks on October 7, and their press release page includes only two entries, one opposing the IHRA definition and one about “anti-Palestinian racism.” Article content Many Jewish Zionists, including me, are highly critical of Israel’s treatment of the Palestinians and its conduct in the Israel-Hamas war. However, for reasons I’ve indicated, I regard the small coterie of Jewish anti-Zionists as misguided. Article content Robert Brym is an e meritus professor of sociology and Jewish studies at University of Toronto. Park Ga-young covers Korea’s vibrant performing arts and the policies behind K-culture Subscribe + From left: Guo Yiming, Lee Jeongwoo Lee and Pin-Hong Lin (George Enescu International Competition) Lee Jeong-woo, an 18-year-old South Korean pianist, won the piano section of the 2026 George Enescu International Competition, the Hyundai Motor Chung Mong-Koo Foundation announced Sunday. The final of the competition took place Saturday. Lee also received five special awards, including for best interpretation of Enescu’s works and the audience award. Cellist Park Sang-hyeok, 22, another foundation scholar, placed third in the cello section on Sept. 7. Established in 1958, the Enescu Competition honors Romanian composer and violinist George Enescu. Held every two years, it features competitions in composition, cello, violin and piano. Lee previously became the youngest winner of the senior division at the 2024 Ettlingen International Competition. He studies at the New England Conservatory in Boston. Other foundation scholars have also achieved notable results at previous editions of the Enescu Competition. In 2021, cellist Han Jae-min became the youngest winner of the competition at the time, while violinist Wi Jae-won took second place. gypark@heraldcorp.com Park Ga-young Subscribe + Sayuwon's first music festival opens with moonlight performance of Beethoven's 'Pastoral' Ven. https://hyperallergic.com/the-polish-pav.text: VENICE — I have spent much of my career as a crip curator and art historian thinking about how access is often treated as an afterthought — the ramp added late, the caption burned in at the last minute, the interpreter budgeted only if funds remain. What startled me most about Liquid Tongues , Bogna Burska and Daniel Kotowski’s installation for the Polish Pavilion at the Venice Biennale, is that access is not appended to the work; it’s the entire epistemology. As a disabled visitor, I did not have to translate myself to enter it; the pavilion had already done the work, in every direction at once. Curated by Ewa Chomicka and Jolanta Woszczenko and produced by Zachęta National Gallery of Art, the installation submerges the visitor immediately. Video projections shot in a Warsaw swimming pool fill the space with aqueous blue, while low-frequency acoustic waves modeled on cetacean marine mammal vocalizations and echolocation press against the body. Sound here is not overheard; it is worn. For those of us whose bodies process the sensory world differently, this is a quietly radical proposition: meaning arrives through skin, bone, and sternum as legitimately as through the ear. At the center is “Chór w Ruchu (Choir in Motion)” (2026), an ensemble of Deaf and hearing performers simultaneously narrating the story of biologist Roger Payne, whose 1970 recordings Songs of the Humpback Whale helped catalyze the whaling ban , in phonic English and International Sign Language. Alicja Czyczel’s choreography borrows the logic of fish shoals: Bodies move as a single distributed organism, with no soloist or conductor. Aleksandra Gryka's score and Magda Mosiewicz’s cinematography complete a structure in which no channel — voice, sign, image, vibration — is primary. Everything is translation; nothing is the original. Installation view of Liquid Tongues at the Polish Pavilion, Venice Biennale The conceptual anchor is “Deaf Gain” (2010), a term coined by Deaf Studies scholar H-Dirksen L. Bauman that reframes deafness as not a deficit but cultural and perceptual expansion. Kotowski, a Deaf artist whose practice has long interrogated language, biopower, and the oppression of phonetic training, is the crucial figure here. His authorship keeps the work from tipping into metaphor tourism — the temporary borrowing of another group’s lived experience as an aesthetic frame — and it places Liquid Tongues in conversation with the two artists who have most powerfully brought Deaf epistemology into contemporary art: Christine Sun Kim and Joseph Grigely. https://english.radio.cz/czech-crown-jew.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК Czech crown jewels return to vault at St. Vitus’ Cathedral Facebook Twitter The Czech crown jewels were returned to the Crown Chamber at Prague’s St. Vitus’ Cathedral in a ceremony involving seven key-holders on Tuesday. Members of the public were allowed to view the valuable artefacts from September 15 until Monday, with the first four days being reserved for schoolchildren. Nearly 37,000 people saw the jewels at the Vladislav Hall of Prague Castle over the two-week period, a smaller number than last year. Keys to the Crown Chamber, where the jewels have been kept for many years, are held by the president, the prime minister, the speakers of the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies, the archbishop of Prague, the mayor of Prague and the dean of the Metropolitan Chapter of St Vitus. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwg5.text: Image source, US Department of Justice Image caption, Prosecutors released CCTV images of the suspect allegedly checking on the secret recorder By Max Matza Published 13 October 2026 A Saudi national has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California, federal prosecutors announced. Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked at the AI firm as an engineer, was charged federally with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. OpenAI said it had discovered a "sophisticated recording device" hidden in their San Francisco office and alerted the FBI. The company said it used its AI models to track that it had been planted by an employee. Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room. OpenAI, the maker of the popular chatbot ChatGPT, said that it has no indication that source code, model weights or customer data were inappropriately accessed or taken in the incident. It said the employee has been fired. According to the complaint, Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. Patel said that the alleged goal was to capture information about the company's AI product. Alfozan has been working as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, prosecutors say. On 30 September, OpenAI employees discovered the device - two days after prosecutors say it had been installed. The device was encrypted, prosecutors said. OpenAI said they were able to use their AI models "to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier". According to the FBI, the suspect used a "productivity tool" and a "chatbot" to research sensitive locations at OpenAI and how to secretly place audio equipment. Chatbot prompts that he is alleged to have searched include "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device", prosecutors allege. He is also accused of using the chatbot to ask about "'build[ing] a continuous audio recorder,' 'customiz[ing] Wi-Fi . . . connectivity,' 'improv[ing] audio and live listening,' and 'encrypt[ing] the SD card'". Image source, US Department of Justice Image caption, The device was allegedly concealed in toilet paper On 5 October, prosecutors say he allegedly returned to inspect the device in the office room. Prosecutors used CCTV camera footage to link him to the scene. That same day, Alfozan left a bag unattended in a different part of the building. A security team for OpenAI opened it to find his wallet and ID, as well as another recording device that was similar to the one found in the office conference room, prosecutors said. Alfozan appeared in court on Tuesday. It's unclear whether he has legal representation. If found guilty, he faces up to five years in prison and a fine of $250,000 (Â£187,000).
